title: Tidy tests/rules: HF-026
how_to_read: Each attempt is one line and a `details` filename in this same directory. Open a detail file ONLY when this index points you at one -- the summaries are here so you do not have to. `caused_by` is what sent the stage back; `changed` is what the attempt then touched, counted by kind. Several attempts in a row that were caused by the same stage and changed no `src` is a loop, not progress.

open.issue: The send-back suggested deleting 'the exact scratch path it recorded when it made the copy', if the design allowed it. It does not fit here. RuleCases never makes the harness's scratch: harness.py's own tempfile.mkdtemp does, and the only record RuleCases gets is the printed line, which is the source of the four spellings. Recording the exact path would take a new harness option or pointing the harness child's TEMP at a RuleCases-owned folder. The second would also move every dotnet/MSBuild/NuGet scratch file the harness makes. Both go past the design and the accepted m1/m2 decisions, which c…

RuleCases C-006 cannot pass on a machine whose GetTempPath holds a non-ASCII character. Its 'engine root <path>' and '<path>\taad3\fitness.py, not from this root' expectations use the raw path of folders New-TempDir made, while harness.py's say() prints them escaped ('\xe9'). Measured: 4 checks fail with TEMP=TMP under 'José Smith'. The expectations could be escaped the way say() escapes, as Get-ImportRuleNames already does for rule names.

Python's tempfile.gettempdir checks TMPDIR before TEMP. A shell that exports TMPDIR on Windows would put the scratch in a folder Invoke-HarnessRaw does not search. Adding $env:TMPDIR to the folders the leaf is looked for in is a one-item change.

%TEMP% on this machine holds 26 fsa-rules-* folders from earlier harness runs, the newest made at 20:54, before this attempt. They are kept scratch from runs that no RuleCases case expected to fail, or from before HF-026 was fixed, and a person may want to clear them. This build did not touch them.

not reached: Whether Windows 11 26200 actually gives TEMP an 8.3 short form for a long or spaced account name. The 8.3 shape used a FileSystemObject ShortPath of a folder made here.
not reached: A real MSYS/Git Bash shell exporting TMPDIR. Simulated with the env var, and it still leaks (left=1): the gap the build declared, which the fix does not claim to cover.
not reached: RuleCases -Case All under Windows PowerShell 5.1. Only C-006 and C-014 were run under 5.1; -Case All ran under pwsh 7.6.
